knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations by Eliminating the First Variable

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}12x-11y &=-33 \\ 3x+8y &=24\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $x.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $x$-coefficient in the first equation is $12,$ while in the second equation it is $3.$ 

If we multiply the second equation by $-4,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $-12,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $12$ in the first equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&12x-11y=-33 \\ &\left(3x+8y=24\right)\times (-4)\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}12x-11y &=-33 \\ -12x-32y &=-96\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\cancel{12x}-11y & =-33 \\ -\cancel{12x}-32y & =-96 \\ (-11y-32y) & =(-33-96) \\ -43y & =-129 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=3.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=3$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =24 \\ 3x+8(3) & =24 \\ 3x+24 & =24 \\ 3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=0,\,y=3,$ which can be expressed as $(0,3).$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3u-10v &=-14 \\ -9u-13v &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The solution $(u,v)$ to this system is $($

{{field-2}}
$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $u$ in the  first  equation is $-3,$ while in the second equation it is $-9.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $-3,$ then the $u$-coefficient will become $9,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $-9$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&\left(-3u-10v=-14\right)\times (-3) \\ &-9u-13v=-8\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}9u+30v &=42 \\ -9u-13v &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $u$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{9u}+30v & =42 \\ -\cancel{9u}-13v & =-8 \\ (30v-13v) & =(42-8) \\ 17v & =34 \\ v & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $v=2.$ However, we still need to find $u.$ To do this, we substitute $v=2$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3u-10v & =-14 \\ -3u-10(2) & =-14 \\ -3u-20 & =-14 \\ -3u & =6 \\ u & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=-2,\,v=2,$ which can be expressed as $(-2,2).$

knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations by Eliminating the First Variable

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(u,v)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3u+v &=-10 \\ 9u+8v &=19\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $u.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $u$-coefficient in the first equation is $-3,$ while in the second equation it is $9.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $3,$ then the $u$-coefficient will become $-9,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $9$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&\left(-3u+v=-10\right)\times (3) \\ &9u+8v=19\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}-9u+3v &=-30 \\ 9u+8v &=19\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $u$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\cancel{9u}+3v & =-30 \\ \cancel{9u}+8v & =19 \\ (3v+8v) & =(-30+19) \\ 11v & =-11 \\ v & =-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $v=-1.$ However, we still need to find $u.$ To do this, we substitute $v=-1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-3u+v & =-10 \\ -3u+(-1) & =-10 \\ -3u-1 & =-10 \\ -3u & =-9 \\ u & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=3,\,v=-1,$ which can be expressed as $(3,-1).$
